subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Hashing and Passwords
description: Learn Hashing and Passwords in one minute.

hook.text: Good websites don't store your password. They store a scrambled version that can never be unscrambled.

buildup.text: A hash function turns your password into a fixed string of characters. The same input always gives the same hash.

discovery.text: When you log in, the site hashes your entry and compares it to the stored hash. It never sees your actual password.

twist.text: If a hacker steals the hash database, they can't reverse the hashes — but they can try billions of guesses.

climax.text: Hashing protects passwords even when databases are stolen — as long as the passwords themselves aren't weak.

punchline.text: Your password, scrambled forever. Only you know it.

quiz.question: How do websites securely store passwords?
options: By storing a one-way hash that can't be reversed into the original password
By encrypting them with the user's email address
By splitting the password across multiple servers
